halló un reloj y un muñeco con forma de pato Vivir en el vertedero es adentrarse en ajenos vertederos íntimos La jaba de mimbre deshilachada tiene la vulgaridad de las cosas comunes aquellas de las que no conseguimos deshacernos las que se adhieren parasitariamente a la vida las que revelan eso que somos Isora encontró la jaba de mimbre hace años Con ella entró en el Sanatorio de enfermos de SIDA antes que muriera uno de sus ocho hijos Con ella atravesó las galerías de la prisión provincial para ver al menor de todos En la jaba acaba de depositar las sandalias un caldero una fosforera Bic El teléfono celular en cambio lo lleva en su mano como un artículo extraviado de alguna civilización posterior como el cristal de Murano hipersensible Hace diez años que la Unidad Presupuestada de Servicios Comunales en Caibarién al centro de Cuba trasladó el vertedero municipal desde la comunidad La Picadora hasta un área despoblada Pero arrojar desperdicios al sitio se hizo hábito y aún aparecen en los alrededores accesorios de oficina útiles de enfermería desechos orgánicos Como Isora otras quince familias aproximadamente han erigido sus ranchos en la ciudadela No hay registro urbano que ofrezca datos precisos sobre esta pequeña sociedad de parias Nadie sabe si fue vecindario o basurero inicialmente aunque da igual ambas cosas son estiércol mugre bajo la alfombra la postal fea donde nadie demora la mirada Isora se posa como un pájaro sucio en la esquina del portón Se apoya en la pared de tablas y prende un cigarro Al morir su hijo seropositivo decidió de una buena vez no dejar jamás de fumar y ahora se quiebra en un espumarajo hediondo cada vez que tose En el rancho de cuatro por cuatro que llama casa vive con su hija María Luisa y su nieto de 14 años A veces no hay agua me dice a veces uno deja de bañarse en días pa cocinarle el bocaʼo de comida a los muchachos El agua no sube a La Picadora Cada tres días llevan una pipa al caserío Pero no alcanza Ni siquiera alivia Desde diciembre de 2015 la Empresa de Acueducto y Alcantarillado en Caibarién intenta reparar las averías en la red hidráulica Las labores de reparación no dependen únicamente de esta empresa sino de recursos equipamiento fuerza de trabajo presupuestos y autorización de terceras cuartas y enésimas instancias Bañarse o cocinar requiere un trámite en caracol un bucle burocrático infinito Isora tiene esa piel fibrosa parecida al cuero Su silueta no es humana pertenece a la fabulación Su espalda no es espalda sino lomo Quizá para sostener los bloques del dolor para echarse los días a cuesta Isora colecciona pérdidas El 31 de octubre de 2014 perdió una bisnieta de 11 meses La enterró allí junto al hijo seropositivo a orillas del basurero El basurero está allí a orillas del cementerio La muerte de los suyos nunca ha admitido la alegoría del viaje Bastan dos zancadas Basta ladear la mirada Para los pobres la tristeza es fragmentaria Una pérdida se disemina en pequeñas penas En teoría un pobre compensa su dolor con el propio dolor que es ya la miseria su estado natural Isora sufre tanto que ni siquiera lo sabe piensa que la vida es solo eso No parece Isora una mujer amarga Extraños modos de la felicidad

For the original Spanish version, please scroll down Si desea puede consultar la versión original en español a continuación de esta traducción al alemán She has never been so lost in an object as she is now Isora Gómez knows that this is a mobile phone She has seen some before She has also seen She has also seen padlocks combs needles cans hangers cups cables ropes But still this object does not trigger memories or a memory from before time Nothing Isora Gómez stands in front of the mountain with new rubbish Her body of 62 looks like after 80 years of exhaustion She stirs with a stick in the rubbish until she sees something she likes. She is a woman with a lot of luck Of all those poking around in the rubbish, she is the only one who has ever found sandals almost her size Once she found a watch, once a doll in the shape of a duck Living in a rubbish dump also means living in someone else's intimacy. The frayed bag harbours vulgarities that we can't part with that parasitically attach themselves to our lives that tell us who we are Isora found the bag years ago With it in her hand, she went to the Aids ward before one of her eight sons died With it in her hand, she walked through the corridors of the provincial prison She walked through the corridors of the provincial prison to visit her youngest In the bag are the sandals a pot a Bic lighter The mobile phone, however, she holds in her hand like a foreign object from a distant civilisation Ten years ago, the authorities of Caibarién in central Cuba moved the communal rubbish dump from the village of La Picadora village to an uninhabited area But it had already become a habit to throw things away there and to this day, office materials or organic waste still turn up there Medical or organic waste Like Isora, around 15 other families have built their huts there No municipal authority can provide precise information about this small community of pariahs. No one knows if the dump or the residents were there first, but it doesn't matter either way it's manure under the carpet the ugly postcard that no one wants to look at Like a dirty bird, Isora stands at the corner of the gate She leans against the wooden wall and lights a cigarette When her son, who had AIDS, died, she promised never to smoke. son died, she resolved never to stop smoking and now every time she coughs, she writhes in a sickening wheeze In the four-by-four metre hut she calls her house, she lives with her daughter María Luisa and her 14-year-old grandson Sometimes there is no water, she says, sometimes she doesn't wash for days to do what little water she has. Sometimes she doesn't wash for days to use the little water she has to cook the children something to eat The water doesn't come up to La Picadora Every three days a tanker comes to the settlement But it's not enough It doesn't even provide relief Since December 2015, the Caibarién waterworks have been trying to repair the damage to the water pipes But the work depends not only on the waterworks but also on resources equipment labour funding and its approval by third, fourth and fifth instances Being able to wash or cook is stuck in a bureaucratic endless loop Isora has this tanned skin that looks like leather Her silhouette looks like leather, but she can't see it. skin that looks like leather Her silhouette has nothing human about it, more like a mythical creature Her back is not a back but a hump Perhaps to endure the pain the days that are hard Isora collects losses On 31 October 2014, she lost an eleven-month-old great-granddaughter She buried her there right next to her son with AIDS at the foot of the rubbish dump where the cemetery is The death of her loved ones could never be described for her with the allegory of the completed journey It was enough to look away For the poor, sadness is made up of many small parts A loss is broken down into many small pains Theoretically the poor compensate for their pain with the pain that poverty itself creates It corresponds to their nature Isora suffers so much that she doesn't even realise it herself She thinks life is just like that Isora doesn't seem bitter Happiness comes in strange guises When her youngest son José set fire to the village shop she lay down by his side and kissed him on the cheek The smell of burning cut the air The son calmed his mother until the police took him away José was diagnosed with schizophrenia Isora visited him in prison her well-sorted misery in her pocket She must be with him She couldn't visit him for a while and he tried twice to get his legs back José needs her she has to tell him about her trivialities light a cigarette and see him smile with his brown teeth Although Isora is a widow she doesn't get a pension She doesn't own her living space because registering it would be another endless bureaucratic bureaucratic endless loop No one comes up the dusty queue up the main street of La Picadora the way to her house She sleeps on scraps of cloth She is made of scraps of others I asked her what she would want for her life "A few cans of water" she replied Happiness is something very private

text: betr „Lebenslang für Guzman“ Leuchtender Pfad erlischt taz vom 91092  Macht Euch keine Sorgen von einem Erlöschen des Leuchtenden Pfades PCP kann keine Rede sein Es muß Euch doch schwer nerven daß mittlerweile auf jeder verfügbaren Fläche im Kreuzberger Ghetto Yeah revolutionäre Städtepartnerschaft KreuzbergAyacucho der Vorsitzende Gonzalo mit geballter Faust grüßt Parole an Parole den Leuchtenden Pfad hochleben läßt und maoistische RebellInnen nächtliche Demonstrationen durchführen um im Rahmen einer weltweiten Kampagne das Leben des Vorsitzenden Gonzalo Abimael Guzman zu verteidigen Abimael Guzman der Lenin unserer Zeit Kein anderer seit Mao Tsetung verkörpert so den Alptraum der Bourgeoisie und den Traum der Verdammten dieser Erde Da erlischt gar nichts Im Gegenteil auf die Glückwünsche des Imperialismus folgt die Antwort der Weltklasse 5000 demonstrierten in Neu Delhi gegen die Verhaftung Guzmans In Ayacucho legt ein bewaffneter Streik die Stadt lahm Guzmans maskierte Militärrichter sind offensichtlich die letzten die Euren und den frommen Wünschen der Weltreaktion Ende eines Mythos blabla Glauben schenken wollen Was die Reaktion oder besser Nichtreaktion von amnesty international betrifft bleiben doch wirklich ernste Zweifel ob die ai VertreterInnen in Peru auch nur ansatzweise bürgerliche Rechtsnormen und faschistische Willkür auseinanderhalten können oder wollen  Gordon Agyei Berlin
translation: Regarding "Life sentence for Guzman" Shining Path goes out taz of 91092 Don't worry, there can be no question of the Shining Path PCP going out It must be very annoying for you that in the meantime on every available space in the Kreuzberg ghetto Yeah revolutionary city partnership Kreuzberg-Ayacucho the chairman Gonzalo greets the Shining Path with a clenched fist slogan after slogan and Maoist rebels hold nightly demonstrations to celebrate the life of the chairman Gonzalo Abimael Guzman. clenched fist, slogan after slogan, and Maoist rebels hold nightly demonstrations to defend the life of Chairman Gonzalo Abimael Guzman as part of a worldwide campaign Abimael Guzman the Lenin of our time No one else since Mao Zedong so embodies the nightmare of the bourgeoisie and the dream of the damned of this world. and the dream of the damned of this earth Nothing is extinguished On the contrary, the congratulations of imperialism are followed by the response of the world class 5,000 demonstrated in New Delhi against Guzman's arrest In Ayacucho, an armed strike paralyses the city Guzman's masked military judges are obviously the last to fulfil your and the pious wishes of the world reaction. As far as the reaction or rather non-reaction of Amnesty International is concerned, serious doubts remain as to whether the ai representatives in Peru can or want to even begin to distinguish between bourgeois legal norms and fascist despotism Gordon Agyei Berlin
